elements.brief_element: The system carries knowledge from ingestion through retrieval to grounded answers.
elements.brief_evidence: “how our retrieval-augmented generation system carries knowledge from ingestion through grounded answers”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstructed purpose describes ingestion, normalization, change detection, chunking, embedding, version-consistent publication, permission-aware retrieval, and evidence-grounded answers. Its flows connect source adapters through publication and retrieval to “Evidence-only answer + citations.”
elements.note: The primary end-to-end architecture and purpose are clearly recoverable.

elements.brief_element: The system must make failed-processing handling clear.

unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The component is labeled “Workers: bounded retry,” and the reconstruction repeats a constraint that retries are bounded.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires retries of transient failures followed by dead-lettering of persistent failures, but it does not explicitly define the retry policy as bounded.

unsupported_claims.claim: A partial publication write makes the entire system unavailable until repair or rollback.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: A reconstructed constraint says, “A partial publication write makes the system unavailable until repair or rollback.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says the partial writes themselves remain unavailable before serving. It does not say all other consistent published content or the entire system becomes unavailable.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The strongest transmission is the version-consistent publication and serving path: vectors, text/metadata, and keyword terms are written to three stores, their versions must match before publication, partial writes are excluded and repaired or rolled back, and permission-filtered hybrid retrieval leads only to evidence-grounded answers with citations.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: The dead-letter recovery loop is missing: failed embedding inputs and attempts are retained, but the board does not communicate that dead-lettered batches can be reprocessed. Secondary losses are the lack of an explicit generation-service boundary and the softened representation of a separate new index generation.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction preserves the complete system shape and all critical online paths: scheduled multi-source ingestion with ACL propagation, parse quarantine, hash-based new/changed/unchanged handling, chunking and embedding, three-store version-consistent publication, parallel hybrid retrieval, asking-user permission filtering, grounded cited answers, low-confidence abstention, feedback-driven ingestion priorities, and background atomic generation promotion with rollback retention. The main operational omission is reprocessing from the dead-letter store; change-notification triggering, transient-versus-persistent failure semantics, the generation-service boundary, and the concrete new-index boundary are somewhat softened. The architecture remains accurate and actionable, with no contradiction to a core flow.
